An August 28 storm ravaged San Antonio.The West Side and the Historic Five Points were hit hard. In the neighborhood, a tree destroyed this home. As parts of buildings sit in the middle of roads, the sun rises. Little more than a month has gone by, and some residents say they feel as alone as they did when they first saw the damage.In response to the storm, the U.S. Small Business Administration is providing federal loans for damage to homes and businesses.“They are intended to be at a lower-than-normal market rate that you will see with normal traditional institutions,” said Gabriel Perales, a public affairs specialist with the SBA. SBA staff are at the Las Palmas Public Library to help people sign up. Homeowners can get loans of up to $500,000, and businesses can get up to $2 million. The deadline to apply is November 9.Many residents would have preferred cash grants. The City of San Antonio provides some money for repairs, but pays contractors directly. We reached out to the governor’s office to ask why FEMA grants were not requested. The office directed us to the Texas Division of Emergency Management.We are waiting for a response.
